_provenance.note: Model INPUTS captured from the save; OBSERVED values are player readings taken in game against this same save.

sources.derived: allocation = stock + inbound + open buy amount. A LOWER BOUND, not an equality: a station bids only for what it can use, so a station whose consumers are unbuilt (MAL-475) or which simply is not buying (TPF-229 helium/ore) reads far below its true allocation.
sources.ingame: read off the station UI by the player - authoritative

hullparts: read twice; unchanged after the efficiency change

EIJ-609.note: Workforce 810 (full) but STARVING: zero medical supplies, zero soja husk, both listed under <shortage>. Modules report efficiency 1.12634 and the production rate follows it, but the ALLOCATION follows 1.0 -- the player reports war-pressure bonuses do not count toward storage.

IFO-957.note: The advanced-electronics module reports efficiency 1.39556 and one module; floor(54 x 1.39556)/720x3600 = 375/h, but the game shows 450/h -- exactly 1.2x. EIJ-609 shows no such factor, so the two rate readings are not yet reconciled.

KWC-232.note: Scrap processors do NOT count toward storage. The player's encyclopaedia shot shows why: the scrap processor's recipe is quoted per unit of scrap (1x scrap metal from 10x energy cells + 1x raw scrap), not per timed cycle, so it has no hourly rate to feed an equal-hours split.

MAL-475.note: Player-owned, no manual ware limits. Player confirms every allocation and rate is correct. Its DERIVED values are all far too low because the consuming modules are still under construction, so the station is not bidding for stock it cannot yet use. This is the counter-example that demotes 'derived' to a lower bound.

TPF-229.note: No buy offers for silicon, methane, siliconcarbide or ore; only a 132-unit buy of metallic microlattice. Derived was wrong on helium and ore, right on energy cells.

WRC-739.note: Stock at read time: advancedelectronics 1,775. Two advancedelectronics modules, neither with a <production> block.
